### S1-1 Policies related to own workforce

Air France-KLM’s workforce policy framework is founded on respect for fundamental rights and internationally recognised principles. The Group’s policy reflects the Universal Declaration of Human Rights, the International Labour Organization’s Declaration on Fundamental Principles and Rights at Work, and the OECD guiding principles. As a signatory to the United Nations Global Compact, Air France-KLM is also committed to its universal principles concerning human rights.

The Group’s Social Rights and Ethics Charter formalises these commitments. Under the Charter, Air France-KLM undertakes to respect human rights and oppose all forms of child labour and forced labour. It establishes employees’ right to working conditions that protect their health, safety and dignity and guarantee social dialogue. The Charter applies to all Air France and KLM employees and employees of their European subsidiaries.

The policy framework also addresses diversity, non-discrimination and equal opportunity. Air France continued its policy of promoting diversity and raising awareness of the need to combat discrimination. The areas supported include gender equality, the vocational integration of young people, employment of senior workers, transmission of knowledge and skills, and the continued employment and recruitment of persons with disabilities.

Compliance Officers appointed at Air France, KLM and Air France-KLM are responsible for pursuing implementation of the Group’s compliance programmes. Occupational health and safety governance is further supported at KLM through a structured process for updating and developing its Occupational Safety and Health (“ARBO”) policy. Twelve occupational safety policies were developed in 2018 with recommended implementation provisions and plans. Five had been approved by the Safety Review Board and agreed with the KLM Works Council, demonstrating the role of employee representation in policy development.

Implementation and performance are monitored using social indicators including workforce composition by age, gender and geographical area; women’s representation among the top 10% of management; recruitment and departures; sickness and workplace-accident absenteeism; workplace-accident frequency and severity rates; training hours per employee; employees with disabilities; and collective agreements signed. The reported social-data scope covers Air France in France, HOP!, KLM in the Netherlands and KLM Catering Services.

For 2019, five employee fatalities resulting from work-related injuries were reported. The reported indicator for fatalities from work-related injuries and ill health was five for employees and five for non-employees. These outcomes reinforce the importance of continued implementation and oversight of occupational health and safety policies. No specific quantified workforce-policy target or 2019 policy revision was identified in the information reported.

### S1-1 Policies related to own workforce

Air France-KLM’s workforce policy framework is founded on respect for fundamental rights and internationally recognised principles. The Group’s policy reflects the Universal Declaration of Human Rights, the International Labour Organization’s Declaration on Fundamental Principles and Rights at Work, and the OECD guiding principles. As a signatory to the United Nations Global Compact, Air France-KLM is also committed to its universal principles concerning human rights.

The Group’s Social Rights and Ethics Charter formalises these commitments. Under the Charter, Air France-KLM undertakes to respect human rights and oppose all forms of child labour and forced labour. It establishes employees’ right to working conditions that protect their health, safety and dignity and guarantee social dialogue. The Charter applies to all Air France and KLM employees and employees of their European subsidiaries.

The policy framework also addresses diversity, non-discrimination and equal opportunity. Air France continued its policy of promoting diversity and raising awareness of the need to combat discrimination. The areas supported include gender equality, the vocational integration of young people, employment of senior workers, transmission of knowledge and skills, and the continued employment and recruitment of persons with disabilities.

Compliance Officers appointed at Air France, KLM and Air France-KLM are responsible for pursuing implementation of the Group’s compliance programmes. Occupational health and safety governance is further supported at KLM through a structured process for updating and developing its Occupational Safety and Health (“ARBO”) policy. Twelve occupational safety policies were developed in 2018 with recommended implementation provisions and plans. Five had been approved by the Safety Review Board and agreed with the KLM Works Council, demonstrating the role of employee representation in policy development.

Implementation and performance are monitored using social indicators including workforce composition by age, gender and geographical area; women’s representation among the top 10% of management; recruitment and departures; sickness and workplace-accident absenteeism; workplace-accident frequency and severity rates; training hours per employee; employees with disabilities; and collective agreements signed. The reported social-data scope covers Air France in France, HOP!, KLM in the Netherlands and KLM Catering Services.

For 2019, five employee fatalities resulting from work-related injuries were reported. The reported indicator for fatalities from work-related injuries and ill health was five for employees and five for non-employees. These outcomes reinforce the importance of continued implementation and oversight of occupational health and safety policies. No specific quantified workforce-policy target or 2019 policy revision was identified in the information reported.
